canonical_topic: Basis spread stays level 2 even when zero
definition: A rule clarifying that the leveling of an input is based on its data source, not on its observed value at a given valuation date.
core_idea: A Texas gas swap remains a level 2 security even if its basis spread to Henry Hub happens to equal zero on the valuation date, because level 1 status requires that all pricing data come directly from the primary market, not merely that the numeric value coincides with a level 1 price.
key_points: A basis spread of zero at valuation does not upgrade a security to level 1.
Level 1 classification requires all data inputs to come directly from the primary market, not just a matching value.
relationships: Refines the Henry Hub / Texas basis leveling example in this same section.
trading_implications: Firms cannot reclassify a swap's fair-value level opportunistically based on a temporarily favorable (zero) basis reading.
caveats: Assuming a spread value of zero means the input source itself has become a level 1 (primary market) source.
